hints: Notice the supply power is $10 \text{ W}$ but the time is $2.0$ hours, so convert the charging time to seconds before using $E = Pt$.
Recall efficiency links input energy to useful stored energy by $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output} / \text{total input}$, so multiply by $0.80$.
Compare your stored energy with the total $10 \text{ W} \times 7200 \text{ s}$ input and check the power of ten is near $10^4 \text{ J}$.
walkthrough: Identify the input: power $P = 10 \text{ W}$ for time $t = 2.0$ hours with charging efficiency $0.80$.
Convert time to SI units: $t = 2.0 \times 3600 \text{ s} = 7200 \text{ s}$ because $1 \text{ W} = 1 \text{ J s}^{-1}$ needs time in seconds.
Calculate total energy supplied: $E_{in} = Pt = 10 \times 7200 = 72000 \text{ J}$.
Apply efficiency for useful stored energy: $E_{stored} = 0.80 \times E_{in} = 0.80 \times 72000 = 57600 \text{ J}$.
Round to two significant figures as in the options: about $5.8 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$. This is option C.

options.A: Too small by a factor of about 3600 because the 2.0 hours was not converted to seconds.
options.B: Too small because time was left in hours, giving $10 \times 2.0 \times 0.80 = 16$ with wrong units.
options.C: Input energy $10 \times 7200 = 72000 \text{ J}$ multiplied by 0.80 gives about $5.8 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$ stored.
options.D: Too large by a factor of 100, from a power-of-ten error when converting hours to seconds or writing the final value.
